Haartzman's Theory of Dimensional Relativity states simply that directionality is perpendicular to the flow of time. Thus if you can control the flow of time, you can control directionality, and by virtue control all of the physical forces. The Theory of Dimensional Relativity doesn't just stop there with its consequences though. Sure, you can walk up wallks, but in order to do that you have to make time flow sideways, which causes a wide range of fascinating effects.

Consider that you decide to make time flow sideways so you can walk up the walls of a building with your cat. Furthermore, let's say you're doing this at the same time that the election results are coming in. It was a tight race between Al Gore and Oprah Winfrey, but the results are finally coming in. Just as time starts flowing sideways, you bend time to quick crossing one possibility but instead cross all possibilities. Simultaneously you end up with fifteen Al Gores declaring victory against thirty-seven Oprah Winfreys. Many of them have even switched parties. You also discover a lot of other interesting changes. Suddenly it's an Ultimate Showdown of Ultimate Destiny style smackdown of Presidential candidates simultaneously laying a smack-down on each other, giving acceptance speeches, and giving concession speeches.

By now, you should have hopefully climbed that wall. As you turn time to flow forwards again, it moves back to crossing only a single possibility stream. And just for a moment, the whole world will have think it has gone collectively mad, at least until Richard Nixon steps in front of the cameras and accepts his third term in office.
